source.title: [Paper] Dictionary Learning Identifiability for Understanding SAEs

record.file_problem: This is a LessWrong post summarizing a linked paper, not the paper's full text. The linked paper's experiments and detailed results are not present here.
record.tranche_reason: The post discusses dictionary-learning theory and SAE phenomena related to the claim, but it does not report a result that tests any of the claim versions as stated.
record.gate_note: The post mentions limited experiments on toy datasets and very limited experiments on real SAEs, but gives no specific experimental outcomes for those experiments. It also mentions dense features and 1D data without reporting a result that measures any listed version. Theoretical conclusions about dictionary learning are recorded under fits_no_version because the post explicitly distinguishes dictionary learning from SAEs.
record.test_reason: The post summarises a theoretical paper on dictionary-learning optimality conditions, which SAEs approximate. It reports no measured result on any version. The derivations about splitting and absorption touch on whether SAE features are canonical (V5). But they concern the dictionary-learning objective, not a model's representation. The post also gives no experimental outcomes, so it does not test V5 here.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The author presents first-order optimality conditions for dictionary learning as theoretical tools explaining SAE feature splitting, absorption and dense features. The author stresses that the work is largely theoretical, studies dictionary learning rather than SAEs, and has very limited real-SAE experiments.
record.recipe_differences: The post describes theoretical analysis of dictionary learning and toy datasets, rather than reproducing the original toy-model superposition method or measuring its geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: Necessary first-order optimality conditions imply dictionary learning cannot have hierarchically related features as local optima.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dictionary-learning (SAE-like) objectives cannot represent hierarchical features, so they convert hierarchies into mutually exclusive features via splitting or absorption.

fits_no_version.finding: In the wide-dictionary limit, dictionary learning keeps splitting features until each data ray has its own atom.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dictionary features depend on dictionary width and split without bound in the wide limit, so they reflect the objective rather than a fixed feature set.

record.problems: The post is a summary rather than the paper's full text. It states that experiments on real SAEs are very limited and that the analysis concerns dictionary learning, not SAEs themselves. It supplies no quantitative experimental results or uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows: the post gives no specific outcomes for the mentioned toy-dataset or real-SAE experiments, and the mention of studying 1D data does not include a reported result.

untested.parts: All parts: no toy-model geometry, sparsity transition or orthogonality measured.
All parts: no capacity or importance allocation in neurons.
All parts: polysemantic neurons are not studied.
All parts: no real-model feature spread or SAE recovery results reported.
Completeness, stability across runs and canonicality of SAE features are not measured. Only theoretical arguments about dictionary-learning optima are given.
A 1D-data toy model is mentioned, but no comparison of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features is reported.

missing.what: Toy-dataset and limited real-SAE experimental results from the linked paper (arXiv:2606.02385) are not in the post. They might bear on V5 (canonicality, splitting and absorption in real SAEs).
missing.locator: Linked paper; post Summary says experiments are 'very limited'

missing.what: The 1D-data toy model of dense features: results are not reported in the post.
missing.locator: Summary bullet on 1D data; linked paper

record.verdict_notes: The source is a LessWrong summary post; the full paper was not read. The paper might warrant re-reading as a possible T5 for V5, since it argues SAE splitting and absorption are artifacts of the objective. As summarised here, it gives no results or explicit argument against V5.

versions.untested_parts: Overlapping, nearly orthogonal directions, sparsity-dependent transition, and regular geometry are not measured or tested.
The post does not test capacity pressure, dedicated dimensions for important features, or feature competition in neurons.
The post does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
No result is reported on real-model feature spread across neurons or SAE recovery of sparse features.
The analysis is of dictionary learning, not SAE features, and does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units.
The post mentions studying 1D data, but does not report a result comparing one-dimensional directions with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: dictionary learning
rows.operation_detail: Derived a necessary feature-feature optimality condition and applied it to hierarchically related features.

conditions.value: dictionary learning; hierarchy defined as lower-level features active only when a higher-level feature is active

rows.measure: Whether hierarchically related features can be a local optimum
rows.value: The post states that such features cannot be a local optimum.
rows.note: A theoretical conclusion about dictionary learning, not an empirical result on SAE features or superposition as defined in the claim.
rows.check: Theoretical derivation, not a measured effect. 'Observed' only means the post asserts it. It concerns dictionary-learning optima, not superposition in a model.

rows.subject: dictionary learning
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed the stability of mutually exclusive features.
rows.value: The post states that mutually exclusive features are always stable.
rows.note: A theoretical statement about dictionary learning; no result on the listed claim versions is given.
rows.check: Theoretical stability statement about mutually exclusive features in dictionary learning. No empirical value.

rows.subject: dictionary learning
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed feature splitting in the wide-dictionary limit.
rows.value: The post states that splitting continues until each data ray has a dictionary atom.
rows.note: A theoretical conclusion about dictionary learning; it does not measure the geometry or capacity claims in the listed versions.
rows.check: Theoretical wide-limit result, which echoes earlier work. It is relevant context for V5 (dictionary features depend on width), but it is not a measurement of SAE features on a model.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
